notes: New: find an address. Click the magnifying glass at the top right, type an address, a town or a place and press Enter: the map goes there and puts a pin on it, ready to plan a flight
The search box only opens when you click the magnifying glass, so it takes no room on the map. The pin lets clicks through, so you can put a waypoint right on it

With Azure Maps, Azure's addresses, Azure's places and OpenStreetMap are all asked and listed together, best match first (roads last unless you search for a road). With the other maps, the addresses come from OpenStreetMap
Can't find a spot by name? Paste its coordinates (in Google Maps: right-click the spot and click the numbers at the top) and the map goes straight there
New: right-click the map (or press and hold on a phone) and choose "Create a flight plan here": a new plan starts with its take-off point on that spot. With a plan open, the same menu adds a waypoint
The flight planner's top row (the name, Save plan and ✕) now stays in view while you scroll its waypoints and weather
